title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act proposes rules to protect U.S. elections from misleading AI‑generated content. It would require disclosure of AI‑created political material, support fact‑checking, and impose penalties for creating or spreading fake campaign information.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a framework for managing and regulating AI-driven physical systems, such as autonomous vehicles and industrial robots, to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability. It requires companies to coordinate with regulatory bodies, conduct impact assessments, and share data to prevent unintended harms and promote responsible deployment.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This amendment to the Federal Election Campaign Act requires that any political advertisement using generative AI to create images or video footage must include a clear statement within the ad itself indicating that AI was used. The goal is to increase transparency and accountability regarding AI-generated content in political campaigns.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to keep elections fair by preventing deceptive AI tools from influencing voters. It sets rules and penalties for anyone who tries to spread misleading AI‑generated content during election campaigns.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes a framework for tracking and regulating artificial intelligence systems that can modify their own code or behavior. The law requires regular reporting, safety checks, and oversight by a dedicated agency to prevent unintended consequences and protect public interests.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a proposed law that would pause the building and operation of new data centers specifically for AI use. It aims to curb the environmental impact of AI infrastructure by enforcing stricter energy and sustainability standards before new centers can open.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act proposes strict regulations to curb the creation and deployment of AI systems that could act independently or harmfully. It seeks to establish oversight, safety standards, and penalties to prevent rogue AI from endangering society.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board that will investigate incidents involving AI systems that threaten national cybersecurity. The board will also recommend best practices and policy measures to protect critical infrastructure and ensure AI technology is safe and trustworthy.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The “Make AI Work for Americans Act” is a proposed law that aims to guide the development and use of artificial intelligence so it benefits American people. It seeks to promote responsible AI innovation, protect privacy and fairness, and boost the U.S. economy by ensuring that AI tools help create jobs and improve public services.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act likely mandates that government or relevant authorities produce a report on the state of AI capabilities and infrastructure in China. The act aims to increase transparency, guide policy decisions, and address potential ethical and security concerns surrounding AI development in the country.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The “Doctors Not AI Act of 2026” mandates that all medical diagnoses, treatments, and patient care decisions must be performed or directly supervised by licensed physicians, not by autonomous AI systems. It allows AI tools only as supporting aids, ensuring that human doctors retain ultimate responsibility for patient safety and care quality.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating an Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the President’s Executive Office to monitor and respond to risks posed by AI and other rapidly developing technologies. The office would coordinate national security, regulatory, and policy efforts to ensure the U.S. remains prepared to address potential threats and opportunities from these emerging techs.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes federal guidelines for AI research, requiring rigorous safety testing, transparency, and accountability before deployment. It aims to promote trustworthy AI by mandating high standards, oversight mechanisms, and collaboration between industry and government.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes guidelines and requirements for organizations to identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with the deployment of AI systems. It also introduces oversight mechanisms and enforcement provisions to ensure AI technologies are secure, reliable, and aligned with public safety and privacy standards.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes creating a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to focus on AI-related risks. It aims to develop guidelines, assess threats, and collaborate with industry and government partners to promote the secure use of AI across critical infrastructure.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee and guide AI-related policy and research. The committee will monitor developments, recommend regulations, and ensure responsible AI use and deployment.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 requires companies and developers to systematically assess the potential risks of AI systems before they are deployed. It sets out guidelines for risk reporting, mitigation strategies, and oversight to protect public safety and privacy.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed legislative framework aimed at governing the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to establish rules, oversight mechanisms, and safeguards to ensure AI technologies are safe, ethical, and aligned with societal values.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 sets rules to curb the environmental footprint of AI technology, requiring companies to track and reduce their energy use and carbon emissions. It also mandates reporting, establishes emissions targets, and encourages the adoption of greener hardware, software, and data center practices.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed AI education into elementary, middle, and high school curricula so students can learn to use and critically evaluate AI tools. It also calls for training educators, developing standards, and ensuring all schools have the resources and support needed to implement AI learning safely and fairly.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to guarantee that AI systems built in the United States meet high safety and reliability standards. It would set up oversight, testing requirements, and reporting duties for researchers and companies developing advanced AI technologies.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a pilot program that uses AI for cyber defense of critical infrastructure. It also contains additional provisions aimed at strengthening national cyber resilience and related security objectives.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a framework for incorporating artificial intelligence education into K–12 schools, ensuring students develop essential digital skills and an ethical understanding of AI. It mandates that schools create curricula, train teachers, and provide resources so learners can responsibly use, evaluate, and create AI technologies.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that aims to ensure that artificial‑intelligence systems used in processing veterans’ claims are reliable, transparent, and fair. It establishes oversight and accountability measures so that any errors or biases in AI‑driven decisions can be identified, corrected, and reviewed by responsible officials.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how and where artificial intelligence systems are used in its operations, ensuring veterans can understand and question AI-driven decisions. The law also establishes oversight mechanisms to audit AI tools for fairness, accuracy, and compliance with federal standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act establishes a national effort to improve public understanding of AI technology and its societal impacts. It provides funding and coordination among federal agencies to develop educational resources, public workshops, and outreach programs that inform citizens about AI benefits, risks, and ethical considerations.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: This resolution states that the Senate emphasizes the need to safeguard religious freedom and respect authoritative texts while ensuring AI systems are transparent and accountable. It calls for policies that balance technological innovation with ethical considerations rooted in religious values.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard people by ensuring AI tools are transparent and not misleading. It establishes regulations that require companies to disclose when AI is used and to prevent deceptive practices in AI‑driven products and services.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to create and submit a report to Congress. This report will explain how artificial intelligence is used to collect, analyze, query, or share information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to boost AI literacy and skill development across the country. It aims to fund curriculum updates, training programs, and workforce initiatives so that people and businesses are better prepared to use and innovate with artificial intelligence.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act aims to promote transparency and collaboration in artificial intelligence development by encouraging the release of open-source AI models and tools. It seeks to foster innovation and ensure that AI technologies are accessible, fair, and accountable to the public and the research community.
